name: Chakchouka
assumptions: Yield estimated from 4 eggs as primary protein source, consistent with 4 craters/instructions and typical serving size for egg-based skillet dish
Total time summed from sequential steps: 2-3 min onion + 3-5 min peppers/garlic + 10-15 min simmer + 5-7 min eggs = ~20-30 min active/passive; rounded up conservatively to 30 min including prep
No wheat, gluten, dairy, meat, fish, shellfish, nuts, peanuts, soy or sesame in listed ingredients or instructions
Eggs clearly listed and used, confirming non-vegan and egg allergen
Vegetarian confirmed per source dietary note and ingredients
Pescatarian compatible as no meat/fish but eggs present
Gluten-free as no barley/rye/wheat/oats and no bread included in core recipe
Sesame left null due to possible cross-contact in spices or unlisted tahini-like compounds but none explicitly present
instructions: In a large cast iron skillet or sauté pan with a lid, heat oil over medium high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add the peppers and garlic, and sauté for an additional 3-5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt, and chili powder. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium low and continue to simmer, uncovered, 10-15 minutes until the mixture has thickened to your desired consistency. (Taste the sauce at this point and adjust for salt and spice, as desired.) Using the back of a spoon, make four craters in the mixture, large enough to hold an egg. Crack one egg into each of the craters. Cover the skillet and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the eggs have set. Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita.
